newsitem.title: TURKEY: Israel's Levy says Syria unwilling to make peace.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Levy says Syria unwilling to make peace.

text.p: Israel's Foreign Minister David Levy said on Wednesday Syria was unwilling to make peace and accused it of supporting terrorism, Turkey's state-run Anatolian news agency reported.
Speaking during a two-day visit to Turkey, Levy criticised Syria in talks with members of parliament's foreign affairs committee, Anatolian said in a report carried in Turkish.
Peace talks between Israel and Syria broke off last year.
Syria accuses Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of bringing the region to the brink of war by refusing to make peace with Damascus and building new settlements on occupied Arab lands.
Anatolian quoted Levy as saying that Jeruselam, a holy site for Jews, Moslems and Christians, could not be the capital of any country other than Israel.

Turkey's Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan, told Levy frankly on Tuesday that Israel must halt construction of new Jewish settlements in and around Jerusalem and withdraw from the occupied lands, in line with U.N. resolutions.
Levy was to hold talks later in the day with Turkish business leaders in Istanbul.
Relations between Ankara and Damascus are strained by a regional water dispute and Syria's alleged harbouring of Kurdish rebels seeking autonomy in southeast Turkey.
